question: Does the checked Zimmerer package supply matching patient/control statistics, reproducible linguistic measures and the same usable original stimulus for a new synthetic comparison?
decision: Published clinical comparisons exist. A same-task, same-measure benchmark is not currently established. Keep M21 main generation on hold. Do not replace the original comic with a new comic and report the old group levels as a matching reference.

sources.locations: Methods §§2.1–2.2; Table 3; Results §§3.1.2, 3.4; §3.4 paragraph immediately after Fig. 1 (journal p. 88): authors explicitly describe the correlation analysis as exploratory due to its post-hoc nature and numerous comparisons.
sources.scope: 30 English-speaking patients with schizophrenia and 15 corresponding Newcastle healthy controls in the cartoon task. Original study also includes aphasia and London comparison groups; those cohorts are not used for the listed SZ contrasts. The clinical measure is an observed PANSS conceptual-disorganization item, while M21's previous interview cue was investigator-authored.
sources.measurement: The misdescriptions counted by the authors include wrong, odd and irrelevant descriptions per total propositions. Qualitative and emotional expression counts (including repetitions) are divided by words. The source within-SZ between-person evaluation composite uses standardized component measures. The M21 E and V differ in both operationalization and aggregation. Pauses require speech timing; ACS additionally requires the source controls’ sequences of coded propositions.

sources.source: Author-posted R analysis and rendered outputs. Read from the immutable bytes fetched during M21, without executing R code or computing individual-level statistics.
sources.how_to_locate: Within the Newcastle regression section take the JointSZSZ predictor row under each listed outcome (not the earlier JointSZAphasia or later standardized cross-clinical comparison). Ref is NCNC. Rmd fits outcome ~ JointSZ + Age, uses emmeans and eff_size with fitted model residual sigma/df, and places the signed group effect in EffectSize. Ratio variables may be transformed; these are standardized model effects, not raw group means or per-person distributions.
sources.interpretation: The positive within-SZ between-person, cross-sectional correlation does not establish a patient-versus-control effect. The latter has a positive estimate and inconclusive conventional test for misdescriptions; p=.100697 does not establish zero or equivalence. Report all three author-posted model contrasts together; the group p values here are those printed, not new multiplicity-adjusted confirmatory tests. The two evaluation-language group effects refer to the separate qualitative and emotional rates. We did not locate a corresponding between-group comparison of the same standardized composite used for the correlation. Negative symptoms and medication are alternative contributors to group contrasts. No longitudinal or within-person change was measured. Confidence intervals for d were not supplied in the extracted output rows.
sources.available_and_missing: Code and HTML establish same-outcome contrasts that M22 did not have. We did not establish a ready-to-use bundle of the per-group raw mean, SD and individual distributions for all required measures in the inspected reports. Do not confuse age-regression intercepts with group means. A speaker-feature CSV is publicly indexed; M21 checked its header. OSF project license metadata had no license. No participant rows were extracted this cycle and permission for reuse or sending participant material to a provider is not assumed.

sources.source: Authors' MacroNarr software repository; complete recursive Git tree response: truncated=false, 23 paths. README, documentation, test CSVs, assets, and source files.
sources.observed: Public instructions describe building a control-derived list of narrative concepts, talk of a future database and label distributed examples dummy data. Root has software licensing/attributions. No separately named Dinner Party eight-panel stimulus, stimulus-specific reuse permission or certified original control proposition-sequence reference was identified in the inspected tree and documentation. Clinical paper identifies Fletcher & Birt (1983) as separate source. Access, copyright and external delivery are unconfirmed, not proven prohibited. No images or dummy/participant sequences were sent to a model.

next_action: Write one finite clinical-evidence brief addressing the original question. Contrast this anchor with Barch & Berenbaum (1997) in a separate patient speech-production task; record exactly which observable pattern each study supports. No new clinical claim from synthetic data.
